reason: The hypothesis relies on evidence from a different alloy (Al0.7CoCrFeNi, E3/E4) for L1₂ precipitation and Orowan strengthening, but no cited evidence supports the critical claim that this reduces dislocation pile-ups or improves ductility in AlCoCrFeNi₂.₁; E1 and E2 show improved ductility via entirely different mechanisms (cryo-rolling/annealing, hierarchical constraints), not precipitation.
premises: Low-temperature annealing of AlCoCrFeNi₂.₁ induces coherent L1₂ nanoprecipitates in FCC lamellae.
L1₂ precipitates strengthen FCC via Orowan looping.
Orowan looping reduces dislocation pile-ups at FCC/B2 boundaries.
Reduced pile-ups mitigate stress concentrations and microcrack nucleation.
This simultaneously improves strength and room-temperature tensile ductility.
